title: Carvacrol@Activated Carbon Bioactive Nanohybrids for Poly-Lactide Acid/Triethyl Citrate Based Self-Healable Active Packaging Films Applied in Minced Meat Shelf-Life Extension
content: Herein by following the spirit of sustainability and bioeconomy the development of self-healable active packaging films using biodegradable poly-L-lactic acid (PLA) as biopolymer, carvacrol (CV) essential oil as an antioxidant/antibacterial agent and activated carbon (AC) as CV’s nanocarrier is presented. CV was absorbed onto AC via a new vacuum adsorption method. The novel nanohybrid CV@AC with a high CV content contained 71.3%wt. CV. Pure AC and the CV@AC nanohybrid were successfully dispersed in a PLA/triethyl citrate (TEC) matrix via a melt extrusion process to obtain PLA/TEC/xCV@AC and PLA/TEC/xAC nanocomposite films with 5, 10, and 15%wt CV@AC or pure AC content. The optimum resulting film PLA/TEC/10CV@AC contains 10%wt. CV@AC is self-healable, it has 277% higher ultimate strength than PLA/TEC and remains ductile and it has 72% higher water barrier than PLA/TEC film. Additionally, it has low CV release rate (k2 value), the highest antioxidant activity and it shows significant antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella enterica ssp. enterica serovar Typhimurium. This film extends the shelf life of fresh minced pork by four days, according to the total viable count measurements and preserves minced pork from the lipid oxidation while it preserves its nutritional value by keeping higher heme iron content and shows a higher level of sensory characteristics compared to the commercial packaging paper.
